sources_considered.why: Primary molecular dynamics benchmarks include B200, GH200, and H100 hardware and explicitly discuss cost limitations.
Primary experiments on H100 nodes cover quantum circuit simulation and many-body dynamics.
The version available before the post documents A100 and H100 execution of non-generative material mechanics simulations.
The described method includes generative diffusion, making it unsuitable as a clean non-generative counterexample.

evidence_items.explanation: The published benchmark documents molecular dynamics workloads on B200, GH200, and H100 GPUs, including a million-atom system. Its purchase-cost caveat is material: demonstrated usefulness does not establish that these are the cheapest GPUs for that work.

receipt.public_excerpt: All experiments use DGX H100 nodes (Section II-D).

evidence_items.explanation: The experiments demonstrate quantum circuit simulation and three many-body dynamics workloads on H100 systems, with scaling across multiple nodes. These are numerical scientific computations rather than generative AI applications.

evidence_items.explanation: The paper demonstrates finite-element material mechanics computations on A100 and H100 GPUs and compares execution with CPU-based software. This establishes another substantial non-generative application.

unresolved_gaps: These records do not measure the proportion of commercial GPU demand attributable to non-generative workloads.
The papers do not separately date each experimental run; the event month records when the demonstrated capability was publicly documented.
